v-la-voile-la-reserve-ramatuelle.name: La Voile — La Réserve Ramatuelle
v-la-voile-la-reserve-ramatuelle.why: One name worth untangling: Philippe Starck designed La Réserve à la Plage, the group's separate Pampelonne beach club — not this restaurant, whose buildings are Jean-Michel Wilmotte's. Treat any "Starck" billing here as adjacency, not authorship.
v-la-voile-la-reserve-ramatuelle.address: La Réserve Ramatuelle, Chemin de la Quessine, 83350 Ramatuelle, France
v-la-voile-la-reserve-ramatuelle.verdict: Take the all-vegetable tasting menu, not the à la carte fish. If the beetroot cooked in seawater doesn't read as more precise and more surprising than the spiced tuna, the cuisine-santé claim is only a garnish — but it will. Canino trained under Michel Guérard (and later Guy Martin at Le Grand Véfour), and the vegetables are where that lineage is legible: light, exact, nothing hidden behind butter.
v-la-voile-la-reserve-ramatuelle.signature: Bluefin tuna rubbed with spices, a long-standing fixture on the menu — and the all-vegetable menu that runs starter to dessert (beetroot cooked in seawater, its leaves fried for crunch, the peel turned into dressing).
v-la-voile-la-reserve-ramatuelle.caveat: La Réserve is an ultra-luxury domain, not a village bistro: expect three-figure-per-head pricing before wine, and dinner is the register the kitchen is built for. La Voile runs seasonally — in 2025 it opened only from 5 May to 12 October; it is in season now, but confirm the current dates before travelling and book well ahead. One disambiguation worth making: Philippe Starck's name attaches here to La Réserve à la Plage, the separate Pampelonne beach club — not to La Voile or the hotel itself, whose buildings are Jean-Michel Wilmotte's. Treat any "Starck" billing as adjacency, not authorship of the restaurant.
v-la-voile-la-reserve-ramatuelle.hook: Michel Guérard's cuisine-minceur, re-rooted in Var terroir: light Mediterranean cooking drawn from La Réserve's own kitchen garden — fish, olive oil, herbs, fruit and vegetables — served under white sails on a terrace above the bay of Pampelonne.

signal_chip.label: MICHELIN ★★
signal_chip.full: Two MICHELIN stars — the second star announced in the 2020 Guide France (27 January 2020) and retained in the 2026 Guide France.

v-beauvallon-sur-mer-by-yannick-.name: Beauvallon Sur Mer by Yannick Alléno
v-beauvallon-sur-mer-by-yannick-.short: Beauvallon Sur Mer by Yannick Alléno
v-beauvallon-sur-mer-by-yannick-.why: Alléno is the most Michelin-decorated chef alive; this is his first-ever beach club, reached by a complimentary eight-minute COMO speedboat across the gulf from the port of Saint-Tropez.
v-beauvallon-sur-mer-by-yannick-.address: COMO Le Beauvallon, 4086 route du Littoral, 83310 Grimaud, France (Beauvallon, on the northern shore of the Gulf of Saint-Tropez, between Port Grimaud and Sainte-Maxime; reached by a complimentary eight-minute COMO speedboat from the port of Saint-Tropez)
v-beauvallon-sur-mer-by-yannick-.verdict: The Saint-Tropez gulf's first Alléno table — a beach club, not a temple. Order the yellowtail tartare with peanuts and Thai basil ice cream, and the sea bass crudo marinated in baijiu with green papaya; if they don't out-plate every rival club on the bay, the 18-star name wrote a cheque the sand couldn't cash.
v-beauvallon-sur-mer-by-yannick-.signature: Yellowtail tartare with peanuts and Thai basil ice cream — confirmed as a house signature by the Alléno group and trade press (Supper Magazine), though not yet eaten in the room.
v-beauvallon-sur-mer-by-yannick-.caveat: Seasonal — open only 24 April to 5 October (currently in season). Gulf-of-Saint-Tropez beach-club pricing; book well ahead. Alléno is the group's culinary director and the restaurant's creator, not at the pass day to day. And there is no Michelin star here — the restaurant opened in April 2026, after the 2026 guides were set; the 18 stars are the chef's, earned at his other tables, not on this beach. Judge it on its first full season.
v-beauvallon-sur-mer-by-yannick-.hook: The world's most Michelin-decorated chef's first-ever beach club — reached by a complimentary eight-minute COMO speedboat across the bay from the port of Saint-Tropez.

v-le-belrose-althoff-villa-belro.name: Le Belrose — Althoff Villa Belrose
tags: Table gastronomique — Méditerranée & potager varois, sur les hauteurs de Gassin
productTags: Table gastronomique — Méditerranée & potager varois, sur les hauteurs de Gassin
v-le-belrose-althoff-villa-belro.why: Coutel is a gardener's son, born in Saint-Raphaël; the old Villa Belrose star ran under Thierry Thiercelin from 1998 to 2014 and lapsed after 2019, long before he arrived.
v-le-belrose-althoff-villa-belro.address: Althoff Villa Belrose, Boulevard des Crêtes (RD98a), 83580 Gassin, Var, France
v-le-belrose-althoff-villa-belro.subcat: Table gastronomique — Méditerranée & potager varois, sur les hauteurs de Gassin
v-le-belrose-althoff-villa-belro.verdict: A clubby hillside terrace that reads the whole gulf of Saint-Tropez in one sweep, with Jimmy Coutel — a Var native, born in Saint-Raphaël, who won his star elsewhere in 2017 — cooking a vegetable-forward Mediterranean menu to match. Come for the chef, the terroir and the view; do not come for a Michelin star, because Le Belrose does not currently hold one.
v-le-belrose-althoff-villa-belro.signature: Coutel's garden-driven vegetable cooking — a Provençal potager brought to the plate, the register that defines him. Gilles Pudlowski (July 2025) singled out the sériole confite à l'huile d'ail (amberjack confit in garlic oil) and a courgette rôtie / pesto / burrata among the standouts.
v-le-belrose-althoff-villa-belro.caveat: Expensive and seasonal, and the pedigree is easy to over-read. The two fixed menus run roughly €135 and €195 (wines included), à la carte about €140–180 (Pudlowski, July 2025). The hotel and its table open only for the season — about 24 April to 4 October 2026, after a winter renovation — so book ahead. Most important: despite the address's history, Le Belrose is NOT a starred restaurant today. The old Villa Belrose star ran under Thierry Thiercelin (1998–2014), then Pietro Volonte, and lapsed after 2019; Coutel's own one star was earned in 2017 at a different house, La Palmeraie du Château de Valmer (La Croix-Valmer).
v-le-belrose-althoff-villa-belro.hook: A clubby hillside terrace with the whole gulf of Saint-Tropez at your feet — chef Jimmy Coutel's garden-driven Mediterranean cooking, minus the star most people assume it carries.

signal_chip.label: CHEF ÉTOILÉ 2017
signal_chip.full: Chef Jimmy Coutel — a Var native born in Saint-Raphaël, son of a gardener — earned one MICHELIN star in 2017 at La Palmeraie, Château de Valmer (La Croix-Valmer). That distinction is his own history, not Le Belrose's, which currently holds no star.

v-hostellerie-berard-rene-sens.name: Hostellerie Bérard — René'Sens
tags: Hilltop family table over the Bandol vineyards — star era ended 2023, house now Maison Bérard / Riva
productTags: Hilltop family table over the Bandol vineyards — star era ended 2023, house now Maison Bérard / Riva
v-hostellerie-berard-rene-sens.why: A hilltop village above the Bandol vines, a family table since 1969 — but the star you came for has walked down the hill. Jean-François Bérard, gardener before he is a chef, put down the constraints of a seven-day kitchen ("Je ne voulais plus des contraintes du restaurant 7 jours sur 7") in November 2023 and now cooks freely at La Bastide des Saveurs. His old dining room, with its terrace over the Bandol vineyards and Le Castellet, reopened in March 2024 as Riva: Italian-Mediterranean, warm, unstarred.
v-hostellerie-berard-rene-sens.address: 6 avenue Gabriel Péri, 83740 La Cadière-d'Azur, Var, France
v-hostellerie-berard-rene-sens.subcat: Hilltop family table over the Bandol vineyards — star era ended 2023, house now Maison Bérard / Riva
v-hostellerie-berard-rene-sens.verdict: The one-star René'Sens described here no longer exists. Jean-François Bérard left the stove in November 2023; the dining room reopened on 29 March 2024 as Riva — Italian-Mediterranean, on a menu conceived by former Ducasse consultant Bruno Caironi and run by long-time head chef Mathieu Gourreau, no star. The house itself was rebranded from Hostellerie Bérard to Maison Bérard. Falsifiable and confirmed: the authoritative 2025 Var starred list (Le Var des Gastronomes) shows no starred table in La Cadière-d'Azur — Riva is only a listed, unstarred Michelin address.
v-hostellerie-berard-rene-sens.signature: Jean-François Bérard's hallmark was garden cooking — vegetable-forward menus built around his own potager, one billed as entirely plant-based, another framed as a walk through the garden, from a kitchen garden Michelin honoured with a Green Star in 2020. That cuisine did not vanish; it walked down the hill to La Bastide des Saveurs, where he now cooks on ephemeral-dinner nights (Wednesday to Sunday) after voluntarily handing his star back. On the old terrace, the honest terroir glass remains a Bandol AOC off the Mourvèdre vines below.
v-hostellerie-berard-rene-sens.caveat: Do not trust the aggregator and legacy directory listings — several still show "René'Sens, 1 étoile," and it is stale; note too that the site rebranded from Hostellerie Bérard to Maison Bérard. If you want Bérard's garden cooking, book La Bastide des Saveurs, not the hotel restaurant. The terrace over the Bandol vines is now Riva — an Italian-Mediterranean table still run by the Bérard family (Sandra Bérard and her husband Bruno Caironi bought back the company; their daughter Marie-Victoire Bérard now directs it), not the outside takeover it can look like. Neither Riva nor La Bastide currently holds a Michelin star.

signal_chip.label: Michelin ★ (2006) + Green Star (2020) — ended 2023
signal_chip.full: René'Sens by Jean-François Bérard held one Michelin star from 2006 and a Michelin Green Star (kitchen garden / sustainability) from 2020, the first year Green Stars were awarded in France. Both ended with his November 2023 departure — he says he handed the star back — and the room became the unstarred Riva; the 2025 Guide lists no star in La Cadière-d'Azur.

v-la-table-de-nans.name: La Table de Nans
v-la-table-de-nans.why: Nans Gaillard grew up under this cliff in La Ciotat, trained at Robuchon's pass and on the Breton quays of Guilvinec, then came home to cook — the star landed about seventeen months after he opened in 2013.
v-la-table-de-nans.address: 126 Corniche du Liouquet, 13600 La Ciotat, France
v-la-table-de-nans.verdict: A Robuchon-schooled local came home to cook. Nans Gaillard, born in La Ciotat and shaped on the Breton quays of Guilvinec, sends out blue lobster and pigeon from an interwar auberge hung over the drop — the Gulf of La Ciotat, the Île Verte and the Bec de l'Aigle rock laid out below, pines leaning into the frame. One MICHELIN star, held in the current guide. Not the grandest dining room on the coast, and it doesn't pretend to be; few tables anywhere buy you this particular cliff.
v-la-table-de-nans.signature: Blue lobster (homard bleu) and roast pigeon — the chef's stated calling card per the MICHELIN Guide. On the à la carte side the tell is a John Dory in a light aïoli with fennel and beetroot; the cooking reads as pedigree Gallic technique tweaked toward regional produce, not molecular theatre.
v-la-table-de-nans.caveat: Not in the Var, if you are strict: 126 Corniche du Liouquet sits just across the departmental line in La Ciotat, Bouches-du-Rhône (13) — the Var's western threshold, and often mis-filed under neighbouring La Cadière-d'Azur, which actually is in the Var. Not cheap and not a walk-in either: menus run from roughly €68 at weekday lunch to about €145 for the full tasting, it is closed Sunday, Monday and Tuesday lunch, and the clifftop terrace is a warm-season promise (the house shuts mid-December to mid-January). Book well ahead.
v-la-table-de-nans.hook: An interwar auberge on the Corniche du Liouquet, pines leaning over the edge, the Bec de l'Aigle and the green island laid out below — and a La Ciotat boy who trained at Robuchon's pass come back to cook lobster on the cliff he grew up under.

signal_chip.label: 1★ MICHELIN 2026
signal_chip.full: One MICHELIN Star, rated 'high quality cooking,' in the current MICHELIN Guide France (2026 edition). The first star was won seventeen months after the 1 September 2013 opening — so early 2015 — per both the restaurant and the chef's own account; Gault&Millau also lists the house.

v-la-table-du-marche.name: La Table du Marché
v-la-table-du-marche.why: Christophe Leroy built a small Riviera empire off this one bistrot, then lost it: after the 2019 liquidation he was convicted of concealed work in 2021, banned from running a business for a decade, and now cooks at a café-gallery in Paris.
v-la-table-du-marche.address: 7 rue des Commerçants (registered/Pudlowski-cited address of the now-closed original; 11 per an unverified Groupon listing), 83990 Saint-Tropez, Var — old town near Place aux Herbes
v-la-table-du-marche.verdict: The everyday Saint-Tropez this card promised — the village-house bistrot Christophe Leroy ran off rue des Commerçants from 1992, tartare-frites and a daily cocotte for a fraction of the port's marquee tables — no longer exists as described. Leroy's company (La Table du Marché, SIREN 384384756, 7 rue des Commerçants) entered judicial reorganisation in 2016, was liquidated in 2017 and struck off the trade register (radiée) on 22 July 2019; Leroy was convicted of concealed work in 2021, banned from managing a business for ten years, and as of November 2024 cooks at the Renoma Café Gallery in Paris. A restaurant may still trade under the name at rue des Commerçants under unrelated new management, but no Michelin, Gault&Millau or curated-journalism source confirms it is open, who runs it, or what it serves. Falsifiable: the 22/07/2019 registry radiation is public record; if an authority-reviewed, legitimately-run "La Table du Marché" is currently operating, this correction is wrong.
v-la-table-du-marche.signature: Historically (per Pudlowski, 2012): steak tartare et frites, a cocotte du jour of daube de joue de bœuf, and a downstairs pâtisserie counter turning out the tropézienne — the format of the now-closed Leroy original. No current menu is confirmed by any authority.
v-la-table-du-marche.caveat: Address never cleanly resolved: 7 rue des Commerçants (the registered and Pudlowski-cited address of the closed original) versus 11 per an unverified Groupon listing. The Leroy establishment is definitively closed (radiée 22/07/2019, RNE/societe.com registry, corroborated by Wikipedia). Any operation still trading under the name is unverified by any authority and is not Christophe Leroy's — he is banned from managing a business until roughly 2031. There was never a Michelin or Gault&Millau listing; the only critical notice was Pudlowski's 2012 blog review of the since-closed original, which cannot cosign a current operation.

v-marche-de-sanary-sur-mer.name: Marché de Sanary-sur-Mer
v-marche-de-sanary-sur-mer.why: Wednesday mornings, under the plane trees along the port, the coast's larder lays itself out before it ever reaches a restaurant plate.
v-marche-de-sanary-sur-mer.address: Allees d'Estienne d'Orves & Quai Charles de Gaulle, 83110 Sanary-sur-Mer, Var, France
v-marche-de-sanary-sur-mer.verdict: A working larder, not a stage-set. The big Provençal market floods the port every Wednesday morning until about 1pm, but the part worth planning a meal around keeps its own hours: the town's own fishermen still sell their morning catch off the pointus on Quai Charles de Gaulle — no fixed days, weather permitting, and the best of it gone before mid-morning.
v-marche-de-sanary-sur-mer.signature: The etals de pecheurs on Quai Charles de Gaulle — the day's catch off the port's little pointus (daurade, denti, merlan, sometimes tuna or swordfish), landed in local waters and weather-dependent; carry it home with a Bandol rose from the AOC shared with the commune next door.
v-marche-de-sanary-sur-mer.caveat: The 2018 crown is a TF1 viewers' public vote for beauty and atmosphere, not a gastronomic jury — and the fame draws crowds: by late morning in summer the plane-tree aisles are shoulder-to-shoulder and the day-trippers outnumber the cooks. The fishermen's stalls, separate from the Wednesday market, have no fixed days; a rough sea means no catch at all.

signal_chip.label: Plus beau marche de France 2018
signal_chip.full: Crowned France's most beautiful market in the first edition of TF1's national 'Votre plus beau marche' competition, decided by more than 3.7 million public votes over four months and announced by Jean-Pierre Pernaut on the JT de 13h on 9 May 2018 (Royan and Saint-Pierre de la Reunion finished 2nd and 3rd). A public-vote television title for beauty and atmosphere, not a food-quality award.
